title: North Thoresby Lancaster Memorial
crew_summary: 8 killed including pilot Flg Off. Thomas H. Morgan, DFC
narrative: On 4 October 1943, Lancaster ED583 of 100 Squadron departed RAF Waltham on a training operation and broke apart in the air due to structural failure, coming down near North Thoresby, Lincolnshire. The aircraft was piloted by Flying Officer Thomas H. Morgan, DFC, an American aged 23. All eight men aboard were killed, among them Sergeant John Hill Rogers, air bomber, who was just 19 years old. The crew also included Warrant Officer John Thomas Goozee, Sergeant Ralph Frederick Worsey, Sergeant Charles Alexander Green, Sergeant Walter Edward James Giles, Sergeant John Alexander Baker, and Sergeant William Frederick Bristow. There were no survivors.

crew.name: Thomas H. Morgan
crew.fate_detail: Killed instantly when the Lancaster broke apart in mid-air over North Thoresby during an engine air test.
crew.bio: American exchange pilot serving with the USAAF, aged 23. Was gaining operational experience with RAF Bomber Command -- a reminder that Americans served and died alongside their British allies in Bomber Command aircraft.

crew.name: John Thomas Goozee
crew.fate_detail: Killed when the aircraft disintegrated in mid-air.
crew.bio: Warrant Officer serving with the RAFVR, aged 22. Second pilot aboard the aircraft.

crew.name: Ralph Frederick Worsey
crew.fate_detail: Killed when the aircraft broke apart. One of three pilots aboard for the test flight.
crew.bio: Sergeant serving with the RAFVR, aged 22.

crew.name: Charles Alexander Green
crew.bio: Flight engineer serving with the RAFVR, aged 20.

crew.name: Walter Edward James Giles
crew.fate_detail: Killed when the aircraft broke apart.
crew.bio: Flight engineer serving with the RAFVR.

crew.name: John Hill Rogers
crew.fate_detail: Killed when the aircraft broke apart. At 19, the youngest crew member.
crew.bio: Air bomber serving with the RAFVR, just 19 years old -- the youngest aboard. Born 1924.

crew.name: William Frederick Bristow

crew.bio: Wireless operator/air gunner serving with the RAFVR, aged 22.

memorial_details:
Name: Avro Lancaster ED583 - Plaque
Type: Board / Plaque / Tablet
Description: Wall mounted brass plaque on wooden backboard. In the centre of the plaque are small engravings of an RAF Lancaster and RAF badge. There is a Latin cross in between the two. To the right of the plaque is a framed newspaper page from the Grimsby Telegraph with a report of the Dedication Ceremony of the mosaic memorial to Lancaster RD583 on the village green. The same Aircraft Group (LARG) also placed a plaque on the village green in 2002 (IWM ref. 54037).
Inscription: On the 4th October 1943 Lancaster ED583 of 100 Squadron suffered a/ structural failure while on a flight from RAF Grimsby, the aircraft fell onto/ the village of North Thoresby killing the entire crew./ In honoured memory of/ [crew names inscribed on memorial]/ Lest we forget/ This plaque was commissioned by the Lincolnshire Aircraft Recovery Group/ and unveiled by kind permission of the Parish Council
Location: On the east wall of the hall North Thoresby Village Hall High Street (B1201) North Thoresby East Lindsey Lincolnshire DN36 5QL England
Grid Ref: TF 29129 98495
Coordinates: 53.467368219368,-0.056202693557
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/77/546/large_ed583_plaque_0.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/77/547/large_ed583_plaque_newspaper_cutting.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/77/548/large_plaques_in_context.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/77/549/large_north_thoresby_village_hall.jpg

The Avro Lancaster ED583 plaque is a memorial dedicated to the bomber aircraft, specifically this marked plane.

100 squadron memorial service (11th November 2002): The North Thoresby memorial plaque was taken to this service at Holton-le-Clay, blessed by a priest, and then placed in the village hall.

The Lincolnshire Aircraft Recovery Group have erected a plaque in memory of this crew in the village hall.

Unspecified Memorial Service: A plaque dedicated to the Avro Lancaster ED583, commemorating its role in World War 2.

external_narratives.summary: Detailed account of Lancaster ED583 (HW-K) from 100 Squadron. The aircraft took off from RAF Grimsby at 1205 to air test the outer starboard engine. At approximately 1250 it broke up over North Thoresby, with debris demolishing the village chapel and damaging houses. F/O Thomas Morgan was a USAAF exchange pilot. All eight crew killed.
key_details: Took off at 1205 hrs for engine air test
Morgan was USAAF exchange pilot with DFC
